correctness.rationale: Kitano--Nakae Theorem 1.1 gives the exact product of numerator Alexander polynomials times the square of the partial-knot polynomial. In the UFD Z[t,t^{-1}], a reciprocal Laurent polynomial is a Fox--Milnor norm exactly when every self-reciprocal irreducible orbit has even exponent; non-self-reciprocal orbit members must occur with equal exponents. A reciprocal square changes self-reciprocal exponents by even amounts and paired exponents equally, proving the equivalence. The explicit 5_2 polynomial is primitive, palindromic, and has discriminant -7, hence is irreducible and supplies the stated odd-repeat obstruction.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification of the classical sliceness obstruction for the newly generalized construction, rather than one isolated calculation. It separates the roles of the inputs: all Fox--Milnor information is carried by the tangle numerators, while the partial knot is provably invisible to this obstruction. The repeated-tangle corollary provides an exact parity design principle for producing obstructed versus unobstructed Alexander polynomials, and the 5_2 tangle makes this immediately concrete.
